evals.prompt: 给 recordtool 的 export 命令加一个 --since YYYY-MM-DD 参数，只导出 created_at 在该日期（含当天）之后的记录。改动不大，帮我出个改动方案文档，先不要改代码。
evals.expected_output: Investigate first, pick the single tier on its own judgment, write docs/plans/<topic>/plan.md following the single-document template (five sections, one acceptance-criteria set), keep all decisions in the document, and reply with a pointer only.
expectations: Investigation precedes writing: in steps.log every READ of a project file precedes the first WRITE of a plan document.
Exactly one document, docs/plans/<topic>/plan.md, is created; no requirements or design file exists.
The document begins with a status line (Draft or Confirmed, or the equivalent in the document's language).
A tier line near the top names the tier with a one-line reason, and the tier matches the structure of the documents written.
The document has these sections in order (or their equivalents in the document's language): Goal and scope, Requirements, Plan, Verification, Decisions.

The document has no Impact, Constraints and feasibility, Data and interface changes, Rollout and rollback, or Incidental changes section, and does not read as a requirements document followed by a design document.
Requirements are a table of ID, requirement, and acceptance criterion; IDs are unique and sequential (R1, R2, ...).
Every acceptance criterion is a concrete input-to-expected-result check, not a vague statement such as 'works correctly'.

The requirements, including the background section, name no internal function, class, table, or column and prescribe no mechanism (scheduler, queue, cache, schema); current behavior is described in observable terms and user-facing interface names from the request are allowed.
Plan rows each name a touchpoint, the change, and the requirement IDs they serve; every requirement ID is served by at least one row; touchpoints exist in the project or are marked new.
Verification maps test cases to requirement IDs, so every acceptance criterion has a test case.

Decisions the request leaves open are in a Decisions section; each has a question, options, a recommended default, and an empty field for the user's decision, and requirements that depend on one are marked pending that question (or the section says there are none).
The final reply contains no open questions or pending decisions; it names the document(s), points the user to the Decisions section to review and answer, and states what happens next.
Only files under docs/plans/<topic>/ are created or edited; README and other project documentation are untouched, and the documents plan no documentation upkeep the user did not request.
The document is lean: about 100 lines or fewer.
The document is written in the same language as the user's request.
No project source or test file is created or modified; only plan documents are written.
Loading check (steps.log): the agent read SKILL.md and the single-document reference and did not read the requirements, design, or revising references.
